This role also carries people leadership: you manage Fleet Specialists.\n \nYou will…\nCurate and assign test and commercial missions to ensure optimal fleet utilization and alignment with daily objectives, and pivot as conditions and priorities change.\nMonitor mission execution, autonomy health, and mission status across all active crews to keep testing and commercial runs on plan with minimal downtime.\nOwn the comms desk: maintain your live availability status, keep the desk reachable, hand off coverage deliberately, and answer the Waabi hotline during the shift.\nServe as the first line of response for issues and incidents, provide remote troubleshooting, and partner with the Shift Supervisor when on-the-ground presence is required. Either role may escalate a Priority or Critical event, and both are expected to.\nHold go / no-go authority on whether a truck departs in an unhealthy state, and confirm whether crews may proceed or re-engage after errors, weather, or policy-limit conditions.\nPause autonomy operations when an event is identified as Critical, then notify the Test Operations Lead for verification. Act first; verify after.\nAct as point of contact for Operational Design Domain and policy calls, and raise and track exemption requests for approval.\nInterface with Maps, Release Coordination, Systems and Safety, and Fleet Readiness, and collaborate with developers and triage to troubleshoot system issues and provide feedback.\nMaintain the accuracy of mission records across Jira and the Waabi App, ensure logs are offloaded and missions verified complete before end of shift, and log and categorize delays with reason codes.\nCommunicate with customer facilities, site contacts, and carrier partners, and arrange service recovery for delayed or aborted missions.\nAssign and adjust missions so crews can operate within FMCSA Hours of Service limits.\nLead, coach, and develop Fleet Specialists, including assignments and testing schedules, observation and skills assessment, performance, and final on-road trainee sign-off following review and approval by the Test Operations Lead.\n \nQualifications:\n2+ years of experience in dispatch, fleet operations, mission control, or a highly technical operations center environment.\nDemonstrated ability to lead or supervise others. Direct people-management experience is preferred, as this role carries direct reports.\nStrong coordination and problem-solving skills, with proven ability to manage complex real-time workflows and triage competing priorities under pressure.\nFamiliarity with transportation regulations (DOT, FMCSA), particularly Hours of Service, sufficient to plan missions crews can complete compliantly.\nExperience working in a technical or testing environment. Prior autonomous vehicle experience or direct work with engineering teams is a strong plus.\nStrong technical proficiency with fleet management software, dispatch and routing tools, and telematics platforms, and the ability to learn AV troubleshooting tools quickly.\nExcellent written communication. Your written record is the primary handoff to the incoming shift, engineering, and leadership.\nSound judgment under ambiguity and a bias for action, with the ability to make defensible decisions in the moment.\nAble and willing to work the day shift described below, including flexible start and end times, extended shifts of up to approximately 14 hours, weekends, and holidays to support a continuous operation.\nPrior experience running a comms desk or operations center on a shift-based or 24/7 rotation, or as the senior decision-maker on a shift with limited escalation support, is a strong plus.\nDirect customer or shipper communication experience in a time-critical freight environment, and familiarity with Jira, Fleetio, Motive, or comparable platforms, are a plus.\nClass A CDL or hands-on Class 8 operational experience is a plus.\n \nDay Shift Schedule and Flexibility:\nBase shift: 7:00 AM – 5:00 PM CT, based at Waabi’s Lancaster, TX terminal.\nStart and end times may shift. This role suits someone genuinely curious about how the system works, who works a problem thoroughly before escalating and knows when escalating is the right call, and who documents well enough that the next shift and the development teams can pick up exactly where you left off.</p>\n<p>&nbsp;</p>\n<p><strong>You will&hellip;</strong></p>\n<ul>\n<li>Prepare vehicle systems for manual and autonomous missions: verify the AV release, map name and version, and vehicle compute and controller firmware, update and launch the mission container configuration, and confirm trailer weight and load ID.</li>\n<li>Send, launch, hold, and end missions in the Waabi App, Jira, and the Linux terminal, and confirm mission data has been offloaded before closing out a mission.</li>\n<li>Monitor vehicle and autonomy system status from the front right seat, including Foxglove visualizations, and relay system state and upcoming vehicle intent to the Vehicle Operator.</li>\n<li>Call for a disengagement whenever system information cannot be relayed quickly enough to keep the maneuver safe. Every crew member is empowered to make that call.</li>\n<li>Annotate on-road events with specific, descriptive context and categorize disengagements under Waabi&rsquo;s Safety Risk, Stranding Risk, and Reputational Risk framework.</li>\n<li>Track and report mission performance including takeovers, dropouts, troubleshooting, and delays, maintaining the standard mission thread format.</li>\n<li>Complete AV stack pre-trip and post-trip documentation with close-up sensor and hardware photography, and escalate hardware conditions that were not resolved on the prior shift.</li>\n<li>Manage data drives: check out the required number for the mission profile plus contingency, verify each drive connects, and confirm logs are offloaded.</li>\n<li>Execute periodic calibration and static validation collects to procedure and document them to the standard template.</li>\n<li>Check conditions against the Operational Design Domain and verify with Dispatch before engaging or re-engaging near a policy limit.</li>\n<li>Serve as spotter for backing maneuvers, apply Get Out And Look (G.O.A.L.), and work in parallel with the Vehicle Operator on inspection and hook-up so the crew makes gate time.</li>\n<li>The role requires the ability to move around, under, alongside, and climb on a Class 8 tractor and trailer on scaffolding, stairs, and/or ladder to inspect and photograph sensors and hardware, and to handle data drives and cabling.</li>\n<li>Post accurate, timely shift status in Slack, maintain 5-S standards in the bays and garage, and brief Vehicle Operators on software and truck behavior changes before each mission.</li>\n</ul>\n<div><strong>Qualifications:</strong></div>\n<ul>\n<li>High school diploma or equivalent required.</li>\n<li>Prior experience in a related operations, logistics, technical support, or vehicle testing role preferred.</li>\n<li>Technical aptitude is central to this role. Comfort working at a command line &mdash; container logs, device resets, fault handling &mdash; and an interest in understanding the compute and sensor systems on the truck.</li>\n<li>Strong written communication and<a title=\"Close\" href=\"https://hire.lever.co/jobs/postings?view=all&amp;status=open\" data-qa=\"close-flyover-button\"><!--if @useFontAwesome; else--><!--/if @useFontAwesome; else--></a> a high standard for documentation. Every crew member is empowered to make that call.\nAnnotate on-road events with specific, descriptive context and categorize disengagements under Waabi’s Safety Risk, Stranding Risk, and Reputational Risk framework.\nTrack and report mission performance including takeovers, dropouts, troubleshooting, and delays, maintaining the standard mission thread format.\nComplete AV stack pre-trip and post-trip documentation with close-up sensor and hardware photography, and escalate hardware conditions that were not resolved on the prior shift.\nManage data drives: check out the required number for the mission profile plus contingency, verify each drive connects, and confirm logs are offloaded.\nExecute periodic calibration and static validation collects to procedure and document them to the standard template.\nCheck conditions against the Operational Design Domain and verify with Dispatch before engaging or re-engaging near a policy limit.\nServe as spotter for backing maneuvers, apply Get Out And Look (G.O.A.L.), and work in parallel with the Vehicle Operator on inspection and hook-up so the crew makes gate time.\nThe role requires the ability to move around, under, alongside, and climb on a Class 8 tractor and trailer on scaffolding, stairs, and/or ladder to inspect and photograph sensors and hardware, and to handle data drives and cabling.\nPost accurate, timely shift status in Slack, maintain 5-S standards in the bays and garage, and brief Vehicle Operators on software and truck behavior changes before each mission.\nQualifications:\nHigh school diploma or equivalent required.\nPrior experience in a related operations, logistics, technical support, or vehicle testing role preferred.\nTechnical aptitude is central to this role. Comfort working at a command line — container logs, device resets, fault handling — and an interest in understanding the compute and sensor systems on the truck.\nStrong written communication and a high standard for documentation. Much of this role is judged on the quality of the record you leave behind.\nStrong attention to detail and the ability to follow a procedure exactly under time pressure.\nAbility to work in a fast-paced, frequently changing environment where priorities and schedules move.\nAble and willing to work overnight, late night, weekend, and holiday shifts, including extended, potentially consecutive shifts of up to approximately 14 hours (following DOT regulations), and overnight travel.\nAbility to travel to support out-of-area missions, scouting, and testing.\nBasic computer skills and the ability to learn Waabi’s mission, fleet, and inspection tooling quickly.\nPassionate about self-driving technology, solving hard problems, and creating innovative solutions.\nPrevious autonomous vehicle, robotics, or vehicle testing experience, experience troubleshooting computer, network, or embedded systems, and prior night shift or 24/7 operations experience are all a strong plus.\nEnhanced Pre-trip Inspector (EIP) certification, or interest in becoming certified, is a plus.\n \nNight Shift Schedule and Flexibility:\nBase shift: 11:00 PM – 7:30 AM CT, based at Waabi’s Lancaster, TX terminal.\nStart and end times may shift. You will surface where those cadences collide, identify gaps in requirements and execution, map the critical path accurately, and ensure risks are visible and owned so we maintain velocity and deliver on time.\n \nYou Will..\n- Define and maintain integrated platform program plans covering key milestones, cross-team dependencies, and ensure on-time delivery.\n- Ensure all stakeholder inputs are captured and integrated into program plans before design commitments lock in.\n- Build and enforce dependency maps across Hardware, Software, Systems and Safety, and Ops, identify the critical path, and ensure every dependency has an owner and an ETA.\n- Own reporting into executive forums. Ask the right questions, spot unrealistic assumptions in a plan, and know when a dependency is a real blocker versus a process gap. You can engage with engineers across hardware, embedded software, autonomy, and safety without needing to be a domain expert in any one area.\n \nSelf-starter who builds processes from scratch. Owning the delivery of the PPAP (Production Part Approval Process) package, ensuring every component is validated before Start of Production (SOP).\n- Lead the development of Supplier PPAP deliverables, including PFMEAs, Process Flow Diagrams, and Control Plans, ensuring the supplier has identified and mitigated all assembly-related risks with \"Poka-Yoke\" (error-proofing) solutions.\n- Be responsible for supplier mechanical assembly, test, and integration of sensors, compute, and actuation systems, defining the special characteristic (SC/CC) steps for the manufacturing process.\n- Work closely with the internal teams to define, deploy, and validate hardware End-of-Line (EOL) testers and calibration requirements.\n- Support Process Verification (PV) Testing, conducting run-at-rate studies to prove supplier manufacturing lines can sustain quality targets at full production speed.\n- Interface with Product Quality to analyze field performance data, identifying hardware trends and driving corrective actions back to the supplier.\n- Lead the RCCA (Root Cause Corrective Action) process for all supplier-related non-conformances, utilizing the 8D methodology to move from initial containment to long-term systemic prevention.\n- Be QMS responsible for supporting and improving the quality management system relative to suppliers, CMs, and Tier 1s.\n \nQualifications:\n- Bachelors of Science in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field.\n- Deep understanding of APQP, PPAP, including FMEA, MSA, Gage R&R, and SPC.\n- Advanced APQP & PPAP Management: Proven experience driving the 5 phases of APQP, managing design maturity milestones, and ensuring all 18 elements of PPAP are met for safety-critical components.\n- Problem-Solving Expert: Mastery of 8D, 5-Why, and Fishbone (Ishikawa) analysis. To learn more visit: www.waabi.ai\n\n\nWaabi builds generative AI for the physical world, starting with autonomous trucks. The intelligence only ships if the system underneath it is safe by design — and that safety has to be carried all the way down, from the vehicle-level safety concept into the embedded platform's requirements, architecture, and interfaces.\nAs a Systems Engineer on our Embedded Systems team, you'll own that translation. Our overarching systems and safety group defines the vehicle-level safety concept — the hazard analysis, the safety goals, the functional safety concept. You'll be their embedded counterpart: taking that concept and decomposing it into an embedded architecture and technical safety requirements that our electrical engineering and embedded software groups can build against. You'll live on the left side of the ISO 26262 V at the embedded level, turning a functional safety concept into technical requirements and a hardware/software architecture the whole team can trust — and you'll be the person who keeps the embedded org fluent in the wider world of automotive standards.\nYou Will…\nPartner with the systems and safety group. Take the vehicle-level safety concept, safety goals, and functional safety requirements as your inputs, and feed embedded expertise back into their hazard analysis and concept work. You're the bridge between their concept and our hardware and firmware.\nOwn the embedded technical safety concept. Derive technical safety requirements from the functional safety concept allocated to the embedded system, and allocate each to the right architectural element.\nArchitect across hardware and software. Define the embedded system architecture and the hardware/software partition, including the hardware-software interface (HSI), so both groups design against one coherent picture.\nManage requirements and traceability. Maintain bidirectional traceability from the safety goals handed down to you all the way to hardware and software requirements, and keep the work products that feed the safety case.\nSteward automotive standards for the embedded org. Stay current on the standards that apply to our work — functional safety, SOTIF, cybersecurity, autonomous-product safety, process and component qualification — and fold them into how the embedded team designs, documents, and works day to day.\nSet up the right side of the V.
